newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates up amid liquidity worries.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates up amid liquidity worries.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates were firmer at midday on Monday over the central bank's recent issuance of NCDs to mop up liquidity in the banking system, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate was at 5.053 percent against Saturday's 4.925 close, with 30-day commercial paper up to 5.00-5.05 percent from 4.90-4.95.

Dealers said the bullish stock market, which HIT another 22-month high close on Monday at 6,938.87, might force the central bank to intervene to absorb some liquidity as Monday's huge stock market turnover of T$115.29 billion, the highest since June 14, showed the market to be awash in loose money.
The bond market was quiet as most investors focused on the feverish stock market, traders said.
Both the 10-year 84/1 yield and the seven-year 86/3 yield were at 5.7800 and the 10-year 86/4 yield was at 5.9150.
